# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform

## Customer Account

- This platform requires registration to use any features (no guest browsing)
- Customers sign up with email and password
- Customers log in with email and password
- Customers can change their password
- Customers can delete their account
- When a customer deletes their account:
  - Their profile information is deleted
  - Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
  - Their reviews are preserved but shown as "deleted user"

## Customer Profile

- Each customer has a profile with: display name and phone number
- Customers can edit their display name and phone number

## Address Management

- Customers can add multiple shipping addresses
- Each address has: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country
- Customers can edit their addresses
- Customers can delete their addresses
- Customers can set one address as the default shipping address

## Seller Account

- Sellers sign up with email and password
- Sellers log in with email and password
- Sellers can change their password
- Seller accounts require administrator approval before they can sell
- Sellers can view their approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- If rejected, sellers can view the rejection reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Sellers can delete their account only if:
  - They have no pending orders (paid or shipped status)
  - They have no pending cancellation or refund requests
- When a seller deletes their account:
  - Their products are deleted from listings
  - Order history and snapshots are preserved
  - Their shop name in past orders is preserved

## Seller Profile

- Each seller has a profile with: shop name, shop description, and logo image
- Sellers can edit their shop name, description, and logo
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can view seller profiles

## Categories

- Products are organized into categories
- Categories can have subcategories (one level of nesting only)
- Each category has: name and description
- Categories are created and managed by administrators only
- Customers can browse the list of all categories
- Customers can view products within a category

## Snapshot Principle

- This is a platform where money is exchanged, so all data modifications must be recorded
- Whenever editable data is modified, a snapshot is created to preserve the previous state
- Snapshots record: when the change was made, what was changed, and the values before and after
- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be deleted
- Snapshots can be viewed by relevant parties (owners, administrators) for dispute resolution

**Product Snapshot Structure**
- When a product is edited, a product snapshot is created
- The product snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images)
- The product snapshot also includes snapshots of all variants at that moment (product-snapshot → product-snapshot-SKU)
- This preserves the complete state of a product and its variants at any point in time

**Snapshot applies to:**
- Products (all fields including images)
- Product variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller profiles (shop name, description, logo)
- Order items (product, variant, and seller profile at time of purchase)
- Reviews (rating, text content)
- Cancellation requests (reason, status changes)
- Refund requests (reason, status changes)

## Products

- Sellers can create products
- Every product has:
  - Name (required)
  - Description (required)
  - Category (required, can select a subcategory)
  - Base price (required)
- Products belong to the seller who created them
- Sellers can edit their own products
- Every edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete their own products only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for any variant of the product
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant of the product
- Deleting a product also deletes all its variants and inventory records
- Deleted products no longer appear in search or category listings
- Sellers can view snapshots of their own products
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Snapshots are preserved even after product deletion

## Product Images

- Sellers can upload multiple images for each product
- Images can be reordered (first image is the main/thumbnail image)
- Sellers can delete images from their products
- Image changes are included in product snapshots

## Product Variants (SKU)

- A product can have multiple variants
- Each variant represents a specific combination of options (e.g., "Red / Large", "Blue / Small")
- Each variant has:
  - SKU code (unique identifier, required)
  - Option values (e.g., color: "Red", size: "Large")
  - Price (can override the base price, optional)
  - Stock quantity (required, starts at 0)
- Sellers can add variants to their products
- Sellers can edit variants (SKU code, option values, price)
- Every variant edit creates a snapshot
- Sellers can delete variants only if:
  - There are no pending order items (paid or shipped status) for that variant
  - There are no pending cancellation or refund requests for that variant
- A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable
- Products with no variants are visible in search but shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management

- Each variant has its own stock quantity
- Stock quantity is managed through inventory history records (not snapshots)
- Each inventory record contains: quantity change (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason, and timestamp
- Current stock is calculated by summing all inventory records
- Sellers can add inventory (restock) with a quantity and reason
- Sellers can subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with a quantity and reason
- Order placement automatically creates a negative inventory record
- Order cancellation/refund automatically creates a positive inventory record
- Sellers can view the full inventory history of each variant
- When stock reaches 0, the variant is shown as "out of stock"
- Out of stock variants cannot be added to cart

## Product Search

- Customers can search products by name
- Search results show products from all sellers
- Search results are paginated
- Customers can filter search results by:
  - Category
  - Price range (minimum and maximum)
  - In-stock only
- Customers can sort search results by:
  - Newest first
  - Price (low to high)
  - Price (high to low)

## Product Listing

- When viewing a list of products (search results, category page), each product shows:
  - Main image (thumbnail)
  - Name
  - Base price (or price range if variants have different prices)
  - Seller shop name
  - Average rating (if reviews exist)

## Product Detail Page

- Customers can view a single product's full details
- The page shows:
  - All images
  - Name and description
  - Category
  - Seller shop name (links to seller profile)
  - All available variants with prices and stock status
  - Average rating and total review count
  - All reviews

## Wishlist

- Customers can add products to their wishlist
- Customers can view their wishlist
- The wishlist is paginated
- Wishlist shows products (not specific variants)
- Customers can remove products from their wishlist
- If a product is deleted by the seller, it is automatically removed from all wishlists

## Shopping Cart

- Customers can add variants to their cart (must select a specific variant, not just a product)
- When adding to cart, customers specify the quantity
- If the same variant is already in the cart, the quantities are combined (not added as a separate line)
- Customers can view their cart
- Cart shows each item with: product name, variant options, price, quantity, and subtotal
- Customers can change the quantity of items in their cart
- Customers can remove items from their cart
- Cart shows the total price of all items
- If a variant's stock is less than the cart quantity, a warning is shown
- If a variant is deleted or out of stock, it is marked as unavailable in the cart

## Checkout

- Customers can proceed to checkout from their cart
- Unavailable items cannot be checked out
- Customers must select a shipping address (or use default)
- Customers can review the order summary before placing the order:
  - List of items with prices
  - Shipping address
  - Total price
- Once an order is placed, the shipping address cannot be changed

## Payment

- After reviewing, customers confirm and place the order
- Payment is processed (assume external payment gateway integration)
- Payment can succeed or fail
- If payment fails, the order is not created and customers can retry
- If payment succeeds, the order is created

## Order Creation

- When an order is placed successfully:
  - Stock quantities are decreased for each purchased variant
  - Items are removed from the customer's cart
  - An order record is created
  - Each purchased variant becomes an order item with status "paid"
  - A snapshot of each purchased product and variant is saved with the order item (preserves product name, description, variant options, and price at the time of purchase)
  - A snapshot of each seller's profile is saved with the order item (preserves shop name and logo at the time of purchase)

## Order Structure

- An order contains one or more order items
- Each order item represents a purchased product variant with a quantity
- If a customer buys 3 of the same variant, it becomes one order item with quantity 3
- Order items can be from different sellers
- Each order item has its own status
- Each order item can be individually cancelled or refunded
- Order items are grouped into shipments when shipped (see Shipping and Tracking)

## Order History

- Customers can view a list of all their orders
- The list is paginated and sorted by newest first
- Each order in the list shows: order number, date, total price, and overall order status
- Customers can view the full details of an order:
  - List of items with: product name, variant, quantity, price, and item status
  - Shipping address
  - List of shipments with tracking information (each shipment shows which items are included)

## Order Status

**Order Item Status**
- Each item in an order has its own status
- Item statuses:
  - Paid: payment completed, waiting for seller to ship
   - Shipped: seller has shipped the item
  - Delivered: item has been delivered
  - Cancelled: item was cancelled
  - Refunded: item was refunded

**Order Status**
- The overall order status is derived from its items
- If all items are paid → order is "paid"
- If any item is shipped (and none delivered yet) → order is "shipped"
- If all items are delivered → order is "delivered"
- If all items are cancelled → order is "cancelled"
- If all items are refunded → order is "refunded"
- Mixed states (e.g., some delivered, some refunded) → order is "partially completed"

## Shipping and Tracking

**Shipment Concept**
- A shipment is a package sent by a seller
- A shipment can contain one or more order items from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (different shipments)
- A seller can choose to ship items individually or bundle multiple items into one shipment

**Shipping Process**
- Sellers can view order items for their products that need shipping
- When shipping, sellers select one or more of their items to include in a shipment
- Sellers enter tracking information for the shipment (carrier name, tracking number)
- All items in the same shipment share the same tracking information
- When a shipment is created, all items in it change to status "shipped"

**Delivery Confirmation**
- Customers can view tracking information for each shipment
- Customers confirm delivery per shipment (not per item)
- When the customer confirms delivery, all items in that shipment change to status "delivered"
- If the customer does not confirm, items automatically change to "delivered" after 14 days from shipping

## Order Cancellation

- Cancellation is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request cancellation for individual items with status "paid" (not yet shipped)
- Cancellation requests include a reason (text)
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the cancellation request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is cancelled and refund is processed for that item only
- Cancelled items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order continue processing normally
- If all items in an order are cancelled, the entire order status becomes "cancelled"

## Refund Requests

- Refund is handled per order item, not per entire order
- Customers can request a refund for individual items with status "delivered"
- Refund requests include a reason (text)
- Refund can be requested within 7 days of that item being delivered
- The seller of that item can approve or reject the refund request
- When a seller responds, a snapshot of the request state is created
- If approved, that item is refunded
- Refunded items restore their stock quantities (via inventory record)
- The remaining items in the order are unaffected
- If all items in an order are refunded, the entire order status becomes "refunded"

## Reviews and Ratings

- Customers can write a review for products they have purchased
- A review can only be written after that item's status is "delivered"
- Customers can write one review per product per order
- Each review has:
  - Rating (1 to 5 stars, required)
  - Text content (optional)
- Reviews are displayed on the product detail page
- Reviews are sorted by newest first
- Customers can edit their own reviews
- Every review edit creates a snapshot
- Customers can delete their own reviews (but snapshots are preserved)
- Product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard

- Sellers can view a summary of their shop:
  - Total number of products
  - Total number of order items (for their products)
  - Number of pending cancellation requests
  - Number of pending refund requests
- Sellers can view a list of all order items for their products
- Sellers can filter order items by status

## Administrator System

**Becoming an Administrator**
- Any user (customer or seller) can submit a request to become an administrator
- The request includes a reason (text)
- Super administrators can view the list of pending requests
- Super administrators can approve or reject requests
- When approved, the user becomes a regular administrator

**Administrator Grades**
- There are two grades: regular administrator and super administrator
- Super administrators can promote regular administrators to super administrator
- Super administrators can demote other super administrators to regular administrator
- Super administrators cannot demote themselves

**Seller Management**
- Administrators can view the list of pending seller approvals
- Administrators can approve or reject seller registrations
- When rejecting, administrators must provide a reason
- Rejected sellers can submit a new registration request
- Administrators can suspend seller accounts
- When a seller is suspended:
  - Their products are hidden from search and category listings
  - Their products cannot be purchased
  - They can still process existing orders (ship items, respond to cancellation/refund requests)
  - They cannot create new products or edit existing products
- Administrators can unsuspend seller accounts (products become visible again)

**Category Management**
- Administrators can create categories and subcategories
- Administrators can edit category names and descriptions
- Administrators can delete categories (products in deleted categories become uncategorized)

**Product Oversight**
- Administrators can view all products on the platform
- Administrators can view snapshots of any product
- Administrators can delete any product (for policy violations)

**Order Oversight**
- Administrators can view all orders on the platform
- Administrators can force-cancel individual items or entire orders (refunds the customer, restores stock)
- Administrators can force-refund individual items or entire orders

**User Management**
- Administrators can view all customer accounts
- Administrators can ban customers (banned customers cannot log in)
- Administrators can unban customers
- Administrators can view all seller accounts
- Administrators can ban sellers (banned sellers cannot log in, existing orders remain)

operations.specification:
POST /auth/guest/join

Creates a new guest session with JWT tokens. Since guests are unauthenticated visitors with no credentials, this operation functions as both session creation and initial authentication. The server generates fresh access_token and refresh_token pairs stored in the ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions table. The operation inserts a new guest record into ecommerce_mall_guests and creates the corresponding session. Returns authenticated state with tokens.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest session and generates JWT tokens for temporary access.

This endpoint serves unauthenticated visitors who need temporary access to the platform. Unlike member/login actors, guests cannot log in with credentials because they have no registered account. Instead, this join operation both creates a new guest entity and establishes an authenticated session.

The implementation must:
1. Generate cryptographically secure tokens (access_token, refresh_token)
2. Create guest record in ecommerce_mall_guests table
3. Create session in ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions table with token expiry
4. Return tokens to the client for subsequent authenticated requests

This operation is public and requires no authentication. The returned tokens enable the guest to call refresh endpoints to maintain session validity.

requestBody.description: Guest session creation input (empty for guests, no credentials needed)

responseBody.description: Guest authentication response with access and refresh tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
POST /auth/guest/refresh

Refreshes an expired guest session token. Requires a valid refresh_token from the request body. Verifies the token exists in ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions table and hasn't expired. Generates new token pair, updates the session record, returns fresh tokens. If the refresh_token is invalid or expired, returns authentication error.
operations.description:
Refreshes an expired guest session with a new JWT token pair.

This endpoint allows guests to maintain their session without re-creating a guest identity. When the access_token expires, clients call this endpoint with their refresh_token to obtain fresh credentials.

The implementation must:
1. Validate the refresh_token exists in ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions table
2. Check token hasn't expired
3. Generate new access_token and refresh_token pair
4. Update the session record with new tokens and expiry
5. Return the new tokens to the client

If the refresh_token is invalid, expired, or has been revoked, the operation returns an authentication error requiring the client to call join again to create a new guest session.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for renewing the guest session

responseBody.description: Fresh authentication tokens for the guest session

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
Implement customer registration with email uniqueness check and password hashing.

1. Validate email format using RFC 5322 regex
2. Check email uniqueness - if exists and not deleted, return 409 conflict
3. Hash password using bcrypt with 10 rounds
4. Create customer record with email, password_hash, created_at, updated_at
5. Create session in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with JWT tokens
6. Return authorized response with access_token and refresh_token
operations.description:
Register a new customer account with email and password.

This endpoint creates a new customer account in the ecommerce_mall_customers table. The email must be unique across all customers and is used for login. Password is securely hashed before storage.

Validation rules:
- Email must be unique (ecommerce_mall_customers.email @@unique constraint)
- Email format must be valid RFC 5322
- Password strength requirements apply (minimum length, complexity)

On success, creates a customer record and establishes a JWT session in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions, returning access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication.

Related operations:
- POST /auth/customer/login for existing account authentication
- POST /auth/customer/refresh for token renewal

requestBody.description: Customer registration credentials with email and password

responseBody.description: Newly created customer account with authentication tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
Implement customer login with email/password verification.

1. Find customer by email in ecommerce_mall_customers
2. If not found or soft-deleted (deleted_at), return 401 unauthorized
3. Verify password using bcrypt.compare
4. If password invalid, return 401 unauthorized
5. Create new session in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
6. Record connection context: ip, href, referrer
7. Return authorized response with tokens
operations.description:
Authenticate a customer with email and password credentials.

This endpoint validates customer credentials against the ecommerce_mall_customers table and creates a JWT session in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions. Returns access and refresh tokens upon successful authentication.

The session records connection metadata including IP address, href, and referrer for security auditing. Sessions have expiration timestamps managed in the expired_at field.

Validation rules:
- Email must exist and account must be active (deleted_at is null)
- Password must match the stored hash

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized for invalid credentials or inactive accounts
- Prevent account enumeration through consistent error messages

Related operations:
- POST /auth/customer/join for account creation
- POST /auth/customer/refresh for token renewal

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials with email and password

responseBody.description: Authenticated customer account with authentication tokens

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
Implement token refresh using valid refresh token.

1. Extract refresh token from request body
2. Validate refresh token signature and expiration
3. Find session in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
4. Check session exists and is not expired (expired_at)
5. Check customer account is active (deleted_at is null)
6. Generate new access token with extended expiration
7. Optionally rotate refresh token for security
8. Return authorized response with new tokens
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token (and optionally a new refresh token). The refresh token must correspond to an active session in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions that has not expired.

The operation validates:
- Refresh token signature and expiration
- Session exists and is not expired (expired_at check)
- Customer account is active (deleted_at is null)

Token renewal extends the authentication session without requiring re-login. Refresh tokens have longer expiration periods than access tokens per security policy.

Security considerations:
- Revoked or expired refresh tokens are rejected
- Account deletion invalidates all associated sessions
- Consider implementing refresh token rotation for enhanced security

Related operations:
- POST /auth/customer/login for initial authentication
- POST /auth/customer/join for account creation

requestBody.description: Refresh token for token renewal

responseBody.description: Refreshed authentication tokens and customer info

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Join operation creates new seller accounts in the ecommerce_mall_sellers table. Upon successful creation, generate JWT access and refresh tokens stored in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions. Validate email uniqueness against both customers and existing sellers. Password must be hashed using bcrypt with salt rounds. Return IEcommerceMallSeller.IAuthorized containing tokens and seller identification.
operations.description:
Seller registration operation. Creates a new seller account with email and password credentials.

This endpoint handles the initial seller onboarding process. Sellers must provide a unique email address and a secure password. The email is validated for format correctness and uniqueness across both the customer and seller user bases to prevent duplicate registrations. Upon successful registration, the seller account is created in the database and a new JWT session is established with access and refresh tokens.

The newly registered seller will initially have a pending approval status and must wait for administrator approval before they can list products and sell on the platform. During the pending period, the seller can log in and view their account status but cannot perform selling operations.

The response includes authentication tokens that can be used for subsequent API calls, along with the seller's unique identifier and session expiration information.

requestBody.description: Seller registration information containing email and password for account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and seller identification upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Login operation validates seller credentials against ecommerce_mall_sellers table using bcrypt password comparison. Check for account suspension or ban status before allowing authentication. On success, create or update session record in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions with new tokens. Return IEcommerceMallSeller.IAuthorized with tokens and seller details.
operations.description:
Seller login operation. Authenticates an existing seller using their registered email address and password.

This endpoint validates the provided credentials against the stored seller account information. Password comparison uses secure bcrypt hashing to protect against credential exposure. Before successful authentication, the system verifies that the seller account is not suspended or banned by administrators.

Upon successful authentication, a new JWT session is created with fresh access and refresh tokens. The tokens are stored in the session table for tracking and potential revocation purposes. The access token has a limited lifetime and must be renewed using the refresh token endpoint before expiration.

The response includes the authentication tokens along with the seller's account information including their current approval status (pending, approved, or rejected). Sellers with rejected status are informed that they need to submit a new registration application.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials containing email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and seller account information upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh operation validates the refresh token from ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions table. Check token expiration and mark expired tokens appropriately. Generate new access and refresh tokens, update session record. Return IEcommerceMallSeller.IAuthorized with new tokens. Reject request if refresh token is expired, revoked, or doesn't exist.
operations.description:
Token refresh operation. Generates new authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows sellers to obtain new access tokens without re-entering their credentials. The refresh token from the request is validated against the stored session records to ensure it is active and not expired. Refresh tokens have a longer lifetime than access tokens but also expire eventually for security reasons.

Upon successful validation, the system generates new access and refresh tokens, updates the session record with the new token values and extended expiration times, and returns them to the client. The old refresh token is invalidated and cannot be used again, preventing replay attacks.

This operation is essential for maintaining long-lived authenticated sessions while following security best practices for token rotation. Sellers should call this endpoint when their access token approaches expiration to seamlessly continue their authenticated session.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authentication tokens.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens with extended expiration upon successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implement administrator registration by validating the request body contains both email and password conforming to platform standards. Check email uniqueness against ecommerce_mall_admins.email field using case-insensitive comparison. Hash the password using BCrypt with a work factor of 10-12 and store in password_hash field. Set grade to 'regular' for initial administrator creation (super admin promotion requires separate approval workflow). Set status to 'active' by default. Create initial session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions capturing IP address, href, and referrer from request metadata. Generate JWT access token and refresh token with appropriate expiration times. Return IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized containing the tokens and administrator profile information including the assigned grade and status.
operations.description:
Creates a new administrator account with email and password credentials, assigning regular administrator privileges by default.

This endpoint allows platform setup of initial administrators or creation by existing administrators. The email must be unique across all administrator accounts. Upon successful registration, the administrator receives JWT tokens for immediate authentication.

The registration process validates email format, enforces password complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters with mixed case, numbers, and symbols), and creates an active account with 'regular' grade. Super administrator privileges require separate promotion workflow via admin promotion requests.

Related tables:
- ecommerce_mall_admins: Stores credential and identity information
- ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions: Records the initial login session with connection metadata

Security considerations:
- Passwords are hashed using BCrypt before storage
- Token expiration is enforced for both access and refresh tokens
- Email uniqueness is strictly enforced at database level with @@unique constraint

requestBody.description: Administrator registration credentials with email and password

responseBody.description: Administrator profile with JWT access and refresh tokens for session management

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implement administrator login by retrieving the administrator record from ecommerce_mall_admins where email matches the request email using case-insensitive comparison. Verify the provided password against the stored password_hash using BCrypt comparison. Check account status field - only allow login for 'active' status; reject with appropriate error for 'suspended' or 'banned' statuses. Upon successful authentication, create a new session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with the administrator's ID, current IP address, request href, and referrer headers, plus expiration timestamp. Generate new JWT access token and refresh token pair. Update any existing expired session handling as needed. operations.name: refresh
operations.specification:
Implement token refresh logic for guest sessions:

1. Validate the guestId parameter format (UUID)

2. Extract and validate the refreshToken from request body
   - Must be non-empty string
   - Must match the refresh_token stored for the guest session

3. Query the guest_sessions table:
   - Find record where guest_id = guestId AND refresh_token = refreshToken
   - Check if expires_at > current time (token not expired)

4. If refresh token is expired or doesn't match:
   - Return 401 Unauthorized with error "Refresh token expired or invalid"

5. Generate new tokens:
   - Generate new JWT access token (short duration, e.g., 15 minutes)
   - Generate new random refresh token (longer duration, e.g., 7 days)
   - Calculate new expires_at timestamp

6. Update guest_sessions record atomically:
   - Set access_token = newAccessToken
   - Set refresh_token = newRefreshToken
   - Set refreshed_at = current timestamp
   - Set expires_at = calculated expiry
   - Set updated_at = current timestamp

7. Return the updated session details with new tokens

Edge Cases:

operations.description:
Update the authenticated customer's profile information.

This operation allows customers to modify their profile details including display name and phone number. Profile changes are applied immediately and affect how the customer is identified in future interactions with sellers and the platform.

**Security Considerations:**
- This operation is restricted to authenticated customers only
- The system enforces strict ownership boundaries, ensuring customers can only modify their own profile data
- Attempts to access or modify another customer's profile information are rejected

**Editable Fields:**
- **displayName**: The public-facing name that identifies the customer to sellers and the platform
- **phoneNumber**: Contact information that may be used for order-related communications

**Data Validation:**
The system validates all profile fields before accepting changes. Malformed or invalid data is rejected with appropriate error messages. The validation ensures data quality standards are met.

**Related Operations:**
- Customer registration automatically creates a profile with empty fields (see Customer Profile Creation)
- Account deletion marks the account as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp. Orders and reviews are preserved for record-keeping purposes. Reviews remain visible but display 'deleted user' as the author, maintaining content integrity while anonymizing the author identity.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement the profile update service with the following logic:

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify the request is from an authenticated customer. Return 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated.

2. **Self-Editing Enforcement**: Retrieve the customer ID from the authentication context. The operation automatically targets the profile belonging to the currently authenticated customer.

3. **Data Validation**: Validate the incoming profile data:
   - displayName: Non-empty string, reasonable length limit (e.g., 2-100 characters)
   - phoneNumber: Valid phone number format (may include country code, spaces, hyphens)
   Return 400 Bad Request with specific validation errors for invalid data.

4. **Profile Update**: Update the customer's profile record with the provided values. Both fields can be updated in a single request or individually.

5. **Database Transaction**: Wrap the update in a transaction to ensure data consistency.

6. **Response**: Return the complete updated profile with all fields (id, customerId, displayName, phoneNumber, timestamps).

7. **Error Handling**:
   - 401: Customer not authenticated
   - 400: Invalid request data (validation failures)
   - 404: Profile not found (should not happen for authenticated customer)
   - 500: Internal server error

Edge Cases:
- Empty string values are allowed (clears the field)
- Same values as before are accepted (idempotent operation)
- Concurrent updates: Last write wins (no optimistic locking required for profile edits)

responseBody.description: Updated customer profile with new display name and phone number values

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of JWT authentication sessions across all actor types.

This operation enables administrators to audit authentication activity by querying sessions from customers, sellers, administrators, and super administrators. Sessions are append-only security audit records that track successful login events with connection context metadata.

**Security and Access Control:**
- Only administrators (admin and superAdmin actors) can access this endpoint
- Sessions are filtered by actor type, user ID, connection metadata, and temporal bounds
- Access to session data follows the Snapshot principle where authentication events are immutable audit trail records
- Session queries respect actor boundaries - administrators can view sessions across all user types

**Search Capabilities:**
- Filter by actor type (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin)
- Filter by user ID to view sessions for a specific account
- Filter by connection metadata (IP address, referrer patterns)
- Filter by temporal range (creation time, expiration status)
- Filter by session status (active, expired, all)

**Response Data:**
- Returns session summary information optimized for list display
- Each session includes connection metadata, temporal boundaries, and ownership
- Pagination supports cursor-based navigation for large result sets
- Sessions are ordered by creation time descending (newest first)

**Related Operations:**
- Session data is automatically created during login operations (POST /customers/login, POST /sellers/login, etc.)
- Sessions expire based on security policies defined in temporal fields
- Session invalidation occurs on password change (section 288), account deletion, or logout
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement unified session query across four session tables: ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions, ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions, ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions, ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions.

**Query Logic:**
- Union query across all session tables with actor type discriminator
- Filter by request parameters: actorType (enum: customer, seller, admin, superAdmin), userId (UUID), ip (string pattern), referrer (string pattern), createdAt range, expiredAt range, isActive (boolean computed as expiredAt > now())

**Database Query:**
```sql
-- Conceptual union across session tables
SELECT 'customer' as actor_type, id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, ecommerce_mall_customer_id as user_id
FROM ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
UNION ALL
SELECT 'seller' as actor_type, id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, ecommerce_mall_seller_id as user_id
FROM ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions
UNION ALL
...
ORDER BY created_at DESC
```

**Index Utilization:**
- Use composite indexes on (user_id, created_at) and (created_at) for pagination
- Text search on ip/referrer using LIKE patterns
- Temporal filtering on created_at/expired_at columns

**Pagination:**
- Cursor-based pagination using created_at timestamp
- Support page size configuration (default 20, max 100)
- Return total count and hasMore flag

**Authorization:**
- Verify caller has admin or superAdmin actor type
- Reject with 403 if non-admin attempts access

operations.description:
Demote a super administrator to regular administrator status.

This operation allows super administrators to reduce another super administrator's privilege level to regular administrator. The operation is critical for platform governance and administrator hierarchy management.

**Self-Demotion Prevention**: The system explicitly prevents super administrators from demoting themselves. This rule ensures that at least one super administrator always remains on the platform to maintain administrative hierarchy integrity. If a super administrator wishes to reduce their own authority level, another super administrator must perform the demotion.

**Authorization**: Only super administrators can perform this operation. Regular administrators do not have permission to modify administrator grades.

**Validation Rules**:
- The target administrator must currently have super administrator grade
- The requester cannot be the same as the target (no self-demotion)
- After demotion, at least one super administrator must remain in the system

**Related Operations**:
- `GET /super-admins` - List all super administrators (must be called first to get target ID)
- `PUT /admins/{adminId}/promote` - Promote regular administrator to super (reverse operation)
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implementation details for demoting super administrators:

1. **Authorization Check**:
   - Verify requester has super administrator privileges
   - Reject if requester is regular administrator (403 Forbidden)

2. **Target Validation**:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_super_admins table by superAdminId parameter
   - Verify target exists and has grade = 'super'
   - Return 404 if target not found or not a super admin

3. **Self-Demotion Prevention**:
   - Compare requester ID with target superAdminId
   - If equal, reject with 400 Bad Request and error message "Super administrators cannot demote themselves"

4. **Minimum Super Admin Check**:
   - Count current super administrators: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ecommerce_mall_super_admins WHERE grade = 'super'
   - If count <= 1, reject with 400 Bad Request: "At least one super administrator must remain"

5. **Transaction**:
   - Begin transaction
   - Update ecommerce_mall_super_admins SET grade = 'regular', updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = {superAdminId}
   - Insert audit log entry in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_logs
   - Commit transaction

6. **Response**:
   - Return updated administrator record with new grade

responseBody.description: Updated administrator with new grade level

parameters.description: Target super administrator's ID to demote
parameters.name: superAdminId

This endpoint allows super administrators to review the complete audit trail of all critical security actions performed by super administrators on the platform. Audit logs capture events such as administrator promotions/demotions, system-level configuration changes, and force actions.

Each audit log entry contains comprehensive information about the performed action including the action type (e.g., 'admin_promote', 'admin_demote', 'system_config_change'), detailed description with context and parameters, the affected entity type and ID (if applicable), and security context including IP address and user agent of the super administrator who performed the action.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering by action type, target entity type, date ranges, and super administrator. Results are paginated and support sorting by timestamp or other relevant fields. This operation is essential for security auditing, compliance tracking, and dispute resolution.

Super administrators are the only authorized role that can access this audit log data. Access is restricted through authentication middleware ensuring only authenticated super administrators with appropriate privileges can view these sensitive security records.

All audit log data is stored in the ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_logs table which maintains referential integrity with the ecommerce_mall_super_admins table through a cascading delete relationship.

- target_type: Exact match on target entity type (e.g., 'admin', 'seller', 'customer', 'system', null for general actions)

- created_at_min: Filter logs after this timestamp (inclusive)
- created_at_max: Filter logs before this timestamp (inclusive)

Sorting options:
- created_at DESC (default): Most recent first
- created_at ASC: Oldest first
- action_type ASC/DESC: Group by action type
- target_type ASC/DESC: Group by target type

Authorization: Only superAdmin actor can access. Check actor.kind === 'admin' and actor has super administrator privileges.

Response includes:
- audit logs with complete fields from ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_logs
- pagination metadata (total count, current page, page size)

Edge cases:
- Empty result set should return empty data array, not an error
- Invalid sort field should fallback to default sorting (created_at DESC)

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of seller registration applications.

This operation provides administrators with visibility into the seller registration pipeline, displaying all submitted registration applications with their current approval status. Administrators can filter registrations by status (pending, approved, rejected), submission date range, reviewer, and seller identity.

The registration flows through three states: pending (awaiting administrator review), approved (seller gains selling privileges), or rejected (with a provided reason). Rejected sellers may submit new registration requests, creating additional records.

Only administrators and super administrators can access this endpoint. The response includes summary information optimized for list views, showing registration ID, submission timestamp, current status, associated seller information, reviewer details (when applicable), and rejection reasons (for rejected applications).

Pagination uses cursor-based mechanisms for efficient handling of registration volumes. Filters support multiple criteria combinations for targeted searches, such as retrieving all pending registrations from a specific date range or finding applications reviewed by a particular administrator.

Authorization:
- Requires admin or superAdmin role
- Regular admins can view all registrations
- No additional access restrictions needed

Sorting:
- Default sort by submittedAt descending (newest first)
- Support sorting by status, businessName

Pagination:
- Cursor-based pagination
- Default limit: 20 items
- Maximum limit: 100 items

Return summary fields:
- registration id, status, submittedAt, reviewedAt
- requester basic info (id, email)
- rejectionReason (if rejected)
- reviewer info (if reviewed)
- business name from associated profile

Performance considerations:
- Index on status and submittedAt for efficient filtering
- Index on requester_id for user-specific lookups
- Consider materialized view for high-volume registration queries

operations.description:
Submit a seller registration request to become a platform seller.

This endpoint initiates the seller approval workflow by creating a new registration record with a 'pending' status. The request requires the user's authentication credentials (email and password) and business identification information.

The registration submission triggers duplicate detection rules that check for:
- Matching tax identification numbers (rejected if matches existing active seller)
- Matching business registration numbers (flagged if pending application exists)
- Business name and address combinations with 90%+ similarity (flagged for manual review)

Upon successful submission, the registration enters the review queue accessible to platform administrators. The seller account's approval_status field is updated to reflect the pending state. While pending or if rejected, the seller is blocked from performing any selling operations including creating products, managing inventory, or receiving orders.

Each submission creates a registration snapshot for audit trail purposes. Rejected applicants can view the rejection reason and submit a new registration request after addressing the cited issues.

Security: Requires authentication. Only customers or non-sellers can submit. Existing approved sellers cannot create duplicate registrations.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new seller registration record in the ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations table.

1. Authentication validation: Verify the requesting user is authenticated (as customer or seller with pending/rejected status).

2. Duplicate prevention checks (per section 461):
   - Check tax identification number against existing active sellers - reject if duplicate
   - Check business registration number against pending registrations - notify if duplicate
   - Check business name + address similarity (90% threshold) - flag for manual review

3. Create registration record:
   - Generate UUID for id
   - Set seller_id from authenticated user's seller record or create new seller entry
   - Initialize status as 'pending'
   - Set reviewer_id as null (awaiting assignment)
   - Record submission timestamp in created_at and updated_at
   - Store rejection_reason as null initially

4. Create audit snapshot in ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_snapshots for the initial state.

5. Update seller's approval_status to 'pending' in ecommerce_mall_sellers if not already set.

Transaction scope: Wrap in transaction to ensure registration and snapshot are created atomically.

Error scenarios:
- Duplicate tax ID: Return 409 with suggestion for account recovery
- Duplicate pending application: Return 409 with existing reference number
- Missing required fields: Return 400 validation error

The response contains the seller's editable profile attributes. All fields are populated when the seller completes their profile setup during the registration workflow. This operation is the primary way sellers can verify and review their shop information before listing products.

Security ensures sellers can only view their own profile data. The system validates authentication, approval status, and ownership boundaries before returning the profile information. operations.description:
Update the approval status of a seller account.

This administrative endpoint allows administrators to manage seller account statuses including approving pending registrations, rejecting applications with explanatory reasons, suspending active sellers for policy violations, or reinstating suspended sellers.

The approval_status field controls the seller's ability to perform selling operations. When a seller is approved, they gain full access to product creation, inventory management, and order fulfillment features. When rejected, sellers are blocked from selling until they address the rejection reasons and submit a new registration request. When suspended, sellers cannot create new products or edit existing ones, but may continue processing existing orders and responding to cancellation/refund requests.

The operation validates that the target seller exists and is not soft-deleted. Administrators cannot change the status of their own accounts through this endpoint to prevent self-lockout scenarios. When rejecting a registration, a rejection reason must be provided. When approving a rejected registration, the rejection reason is cleared.

The approval status change is recorded in the audit log for compliance purposes. The operation updates the updated_at timestamp to reflect the modification time.
operations.name: updateStatus

Update the seller account's approval_status field in the ecommerce_mall_sellers table.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate that the authenticated actor is an administrator (admin or superAdmin).
2. Parse the sellerId path parameter as UUID and find the seller record.
3. Validate the seller exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).
4. Prevent administrators from modifying their own account status.
5. Validate the requested approval_status value is one of: approved, rejected, suspended.
6. If rejecting, validate rejection_reason is provided in the registration record.
7. Update the approval_status field to the new value.
8. Update the updated_at timestamp to current time.
9. Create an entry in the admin audit log recording this status change.
10. Return the updated seller entity.

Business rules:
- Only administrators can modify seller approval status.
- Cannot modify a soft-deleted seller account.
- Cannot self-modify (admin cannot change their own seller status if they are also a seller).
- Approval status transitions follow valid state machine: pending→approved, pending→rejected, approved→suspended, suspended→approved.
- When rejecting, a reason is required and stored in the seller_registration record.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of profile snapshots for a specific seller.

This operation provides access to the complete audit history of a seller's profile changes. Each snapshot captures the state of the seller's shop profile (shop name, description, and logo) at a specific point in time when a modification occurred.

**Access Control:**
- Sellers can view their own profile snapshot history
- Administrators can view snapshots for any seller to investigate disputes

**Snapshot Content:**
Each snapshot entry includes:
- The complete profile state (shop name, shop description, logo image URL)
- The timestamp when this snapshot was created
- Reference to the seller whose profile is captured

Snapshots are immutable records that serve as the official audit trail for the platform. When a seller edits their profile, the system automatically creates a new snapshot preserving the previous state.

**Pagination Support:**
The operation supports cursor-based pagination to efficiently navigate through potentially large snapshot histories. Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order (newest first).

**Related Operations:**
- `GET /sellers/{sellerId}` - Retrieves the current seller profile
- `PUT /sellers/{sellerId}/profile` - Updates seller profile (triggers new snapshot creation)
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query ecommerce_mall_seller_profile_snapshots table filtering by seller_id path parameter. Apply optional filters from request body including date range (created_at). Sort results by created_at in descending order (newest snapshots first). Apply cursor-based pagination as specified in the request. Return paginated results with snapshot details including id, seller_id, shop_name, shop_description, logo_image_url, and created_at. Authorization check: verify caller is the seller themselves or has admin privileges.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of seller profile snapshots ordered by creation time (newest first)

parameters.description: UUID of the seller whose profile snapshots are being retrieved
parameters.name: sellerId

requestBody.description: Pagination and filtering criteria for retrieving seller profile snapshots

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific seller profile snapshot by ID.

This operation returns a single immutable snapshot capturing the state of a seller's shop profile at a specific point in time. Each snapshot preserves the complete profile state including shop name, shop description, and logo image URL as they existed when the snapshot was created.

Sellers can view their own profile snapshots to track how their shop information has evolved over time. Administrators can access any seller's snapshots for dispute investigation and resolution purposes. The snapshot data includes the timestamp of when the profile state was captured, enabling temporal verification of what information was displayed to customers at specific points.

Snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted. They remain accessible indefinitely, even after the seller account is deleted, to support legal compliance and audit requirements. The snapshot also includes a reference to the seller entity, allowing verification of the snapshot's ownership.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_seller_profile_snapshots table by primary key (snapshotId).

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the snapshotId parameter is a valid UUID format
2. Query the snapshot record by id = snapshotId
3. Verify the snapshot exists, return 404 if not found
4. Verify the requesting user has permission to view this snapshot:
   - Sellers can view their own snapshots (snapshot.seller_id = requesting seller's id)
   - Administrators can view any seller's snapshots
5. Return 403 Forbidden if unauthorized
6. Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers table to populate the seller relation if the response type includes nested seller data
7. Return the complete snapshot entity with all fields: id, sellerId, shopName, shopDescription, logoImageUrl, createdAt, and the seller relation

Edge cases:
- Snapshot ID not found → 404 Not Found
- Requester is a different seller (not the snapshot owner and not admin) → 403 Forbidden
- Database consistency issue where snapshot.seller_id doesn't match path sellerId → still return the snapshot as the primary key lookup is authoritative

responseBody.description: Complete seller profile snapshot with all captured fields

parameters.description: ID of the seller whose snapshot is being retrieved
parameters.name: sellerId

parameters.description: ID of the specific snapshot to retrieve
parameters.name: snapshotId

Sellers can use this endpoint to monitor their registration status over time, view rejection feedback from administrators, and track the progress of re-submitted applications. The response includes summary information optimized for list displays while preserving key details about each registration attempt.

Return paginated results with cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of registration history.

Retrieve a specific seller registration record by its unique identifier.

Seller registrations track the approval workflow for users who wish to become sellers on the platform. When a user submits a registration request, it enters a pending state awaiting administrator review. Administrators can approve or reject registrations, and rejected sellers can view the rejection reason and submit new requests.

This operation returns the complete registration details including the current status (pending, approved, or rejected), submission timestamp, rejection reason (if applicable), and associated snapshots capturing the state changes for audit purposes.

The registration record includes relations to the seller profile and snapshots that preserve the shop information submitted at the time of registration. This ensures historical accuracy even if the seller later updates their profile.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to the seller who submitted the registration and administrators who need to review registration details.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrator promotion requests.

This operation allows super administrators to search and view promotion requests submitted by registered users (customers or sellers) seeking elevated privileges to become administrators. The requests progress through a lifecycle from pending to approved or rejected status.

The endpoint supports filtering by request status (pending, approved, rejected) and requester type to help administrators efficiently locate requests requiring review. Each request includes the submitter's reason for seeking administrative access, the current status, and audit timestamps indicating when the request was submitted and when it was reviewed (if processed).

Super administrators use this operation to identify pending requests for approval or rejection actions. The response provides summary information optimized for list display while full details can be retrieved via the GET endpoint for individual requests.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests table with support for complex filtering and pagination.

**Query Logic:**
- Base query selects from ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests joined with polymorphic requester tables (customers or sellers) and reviewer (admins) when available.

**Filter Capabilities:**
- status: Filter by request lifecycle state "pending", "approved", or "rejected"
- requesterType: Filter by typeof requester - "customer" or "seller"
- requesterId: Filter by specific requester user ID
- reviewerId: Filter by specific reviewer (super admin) who processed the request
- submittedAtFrom/submittedAtTo: Date range filtering for request submission
- reviewedAtFrom/reviewedAtTo: Date range filtering for review completion

**Sorting:**
- Default sort by submittedAt desc (newest requests first)
- Alternative sorts: status asc/desc, reviewedAt desc, requester name

**Pagination:**
- Cursor-based pagination for efficient large result sets
- Configurable page size (default 20, max 100)

**Authorization:**
- Requires super administrator authentication
- Regular administrators are denied access to this endpoint

**Response Data:**
Include summary fields: id, reason (truncated), status, submittedAt, reviewedAt, requester type, requester display name, reviewer display name when available.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrator promotion request summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering administrator promotion requests

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator promotion request.

This endpoint allows super administrators to view a single promotion request by its unique identifier. The response includes the complete request details such as the current status (pending, approved, or rejected), the reason provided by the requester explaining why they seek administrative privileges, any rejection reason recorded by the reviewing super administrator, and timestamps for creation and last update.

The requester information is included polymorphically - it can be either a Customer or Seller who submitted the request. This supports the business rule that any registered user (customer or seller) may submit a request to become an administrator.

Security Note: Only super administrators are authorized to access this endpoint. Regular administrators cannot view promotion request details or perform review actions. This ensures exclusive review authority at the highest administrative level as required by the platform's security model.

The response includes the requester's identity, the reason for the promotion request, the current status in the review workflow, and audit information. If the request has been rejected, the rejection reason is also included.

operations.description:
Creates a new administrator promotion request submitted by authenticated users (customers or sellers) seeking elevated privileges to become administrators.

This endpoint allows registered platform users to petition for administrative access. Users must provide a compelling reason explaining their qualifications, experience, and motivation for requesting administrator status. The reason is recorded for future review by super administrators.

Upon creation, the promotion request is initialized with 'pending' status and awaits review by a super administrator. Each user is allowed only one pending promotion request at any given time - attempting to submit while already having a pending request will be rejected.

The request is associated with the authenticated user through the appropriate polymorphic subtype (customer or seller). Once submitted, super administrators can view the pending request list, review the details including the reason, and either approve or reject the request.

This operation requires authentication at the customer or seller level. Regular administrators cannot submit promotion requests as they already possess administrative privileges.

Related entities include the requester's user account and the reviewer who will ultimately process the request.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Verify the authenticated user is a customer or seller (not already an administrator). Check that no pending promotion request already exists for this user (query the appropriate subtype table by customer_id or seller_id joined with admin_promotion_requests where status='pending'). Validate the 'reason' field is provided and meets minimum length requirements (non-empty string). Create a new record in ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests with status='pending', the provided reason, and null reviewer_id/rejection_reason. Create the corresponding subtype record (admin_promotion_request_customers or admin_promotion_request_sellers) linking the request to the user. Return the complete created entity with all fields including system-generated id, timestamps, and initial status.

responseBody.description: The newly created administrator promotion request entity with all fields populated including system-generated id and timestamps.

requestBody.description: Creation data containing the user's reason for requesting administrator privileges.

operations.description:
Update an administrator promotion request by approving or rejecting it.

This endpoint is exclusively available to super administrators for reviewing and processing pending promotion requests submitted by customers or sellers seeking administrative privileges.

When a super administrator approves a request:
- The request status changes from "pending" to "approved"
- The requesting user (customer or seller) is granted regular administrator privileges
- The reviewer_id is set to the approving super administrator
- A snapshot is created to preserve the state change for audit purposes

When a super administrator rejects a request:
- The status changes from "pending" to "rejected"
- The rejection_reason field must contain an explanation for the rejection
- The requesting user remains as customer or seller but may submit a new promotion request
- A snapshot is created to preserve the rejection state

Validation ensures:
- Only requests with "pending" status can be updated
- The promotionRequestId must reference an existing, non-deleted request
- Rejection requires a non-empty rejection_reason
- Super administrator authorization is required

Related operations:
- POST /admin-promotion-requests to submit a new promotion request
- GET /admin-promotion-requests to list pending requests (super admin only)
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement the promotion request review process for super administrators.

Service Logic:
1. Verify the authenticated user has superAdmin role (authorization check)
2. Retrieve the promotion request by promotionRequestId
3. Validate the request exists and status is "pending"
4. Extract status and rejection_reason from request body
5. If rejecting, validate rejection_reason is non-empty
6. Start a database transaction
7. Update the promotion request:
   - Set status to approved or rejected
   - Set reviewer_id to the current super administrator's ID
   - Set rejection_reason (null if approved, required value if rejected)
   - Update updated_at timestamp
8. If approved, create an admin record linking to the requester's customer/seller account
9. Create a snapshot record in ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots to preserve the state change
10. Commit the transaction
11. Return the updated promotion request

Error Handling:
- 404 if promotionRequestId not found
- 400 if request status is not "pending"
- 400 if rejecting without rejection_reason
- 400 if invalid status value provided
- 403 if user is not super administrator

The response includes the complete updated promotion request with all fields.

responseBody.description: Updated administrator promotion request with all current values

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the promotion request to review and update
parameters.name: promotionRequestId

requestBody.description: Update information for the promotion request including the decision status and optional rejection reason

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of immutable snapshots for a specific admin promotion request.

This endpoint returns the complete audit trail of state changes for an admin promotion request, including who reviewed it, what status changed, and when the change occurred. Snapshots are created automatically by the system whenever a promotion request's status changes (e.g., from pending to approved or rejected).

**Access Control:** Only authorized users with appropriate permissions can access these snapshots. Typically, the requesting customer/seller (to view their own request history) and administrators (to review audit trails) have access. The requester's identity is verified against the promotion request's requester_id field.

**Business Purpose:** These snapshots provide an immutable record of administrative promotion decisions. They are essential for:
- Compliance auditing and security reviews
- Dispute resolution regarding promotion/rejection decisions
- Historical analysis of administrative privilege changes
- Accountability for super administrator decisions

**Snapshot Contents:** Each snapshot captures:
- The previous and new status values (pending, approved, rejected)
- The administrators who performed the previous and current review actions
- The rejection or approval reasons provided by reviewers
- The exact timestamp when the state change occurred

**Important:** Snapshots are permanent records that cannot be modified or deleted (sections 409, 410, 319). They remain accessible even if the parent promotion request is eventually deleted.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implementation must query the ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots table filtered by admin_promotion_request_id = promotionRequestId.

**Database Query:**
- Join with ecommerce_mall_admins to retrieve administrator details for previousReviewer and newReviewer
- Filter: WHERE admin_promotion_request_id = {promotionRequestId}
- Order: ORDER BY created_at ASC (chronological order to show history progression)
- Pagination: Cursor-based or offset-based with configurable page size

**Authorization Logic:**
1. Verify the requesting user has permission to view this promotion request's snapshots
2. Allow if user is the requester of the promotion request
3. Allow if user is an administrator (admin or superAdmin role)
4. Deny access for other users

**Response Structure:**
- Return paginated results using IPageIEcommerceMallAdminPromotionRequestSnapshot.Summary
- Include snapshot ID, timestamps, previous/new status, reviewer information, and reasons
- Resolve previousReviewer and newReviewer details from the admins table

**Edge Cases:**
- Empty list if promotion request has no status changes yet (only initial state)
- Handle case where previous_reviewer_id is null (first state change)
- Ensure proper handling of timezone in created_at timestamps

responseBody.description: Paginated list of admin promotion request snapshots with reviewer details and status transitions.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of immutable snapshots for a specific admin promotion request.

This endpoint returns the complete audit trail of state changes for an admin promotion request, including who reviewed it, what status changed, and when the change occurred. Snapshots are created automatically by the system whenever a promotion request's status changes (e.g., from pending to approved or rejected).

**Access Control:** Only authorized users with appropriate permissions can access these snapshots. Typically, the requesting customer/seller (to view their own request history) and administrators (to review audit trails) have access. The requester's identity is verified against the promotion request's requester_id field.

**Business Purpose:** These snapshots provide an immutable record of administrative promotion decisions. They are essential for:
- Compliance auditing and security reviews
- Dispute resolution regarding promotion/rejection decisions
- Historical analysis of administrative privilege changes
- Accountability for super administrator decisions

**Snapshot Contents:** Each snapshot captures:
- The previous and new status values (pending, approved, rejected)
- The administrators who performed the previous and current review actions
- The rejection or approval reasons provided by reviewers
- The exact timestamp when the state change occurred

**Important:** Snapshots are permanent records that cannot be modified or deleted (sections 409, 410, 319). They remain accessible even if the parent promotion request is eventually deleted.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implementation must query the ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots table filtered by admin_promotion_request_id = promotionRequestId.

**Database Query:**
- Join with ecommerce_mall_admins to retrieve administrator details for previousReviewer and newReviewer
- Filter: WHERE admin_promotion_request_id = {promotionRequestId}
- Order: ORDER BY created_at ASC (chronological order to show history progression)
- Pagination: Cursor-based or offset-based with configurable page size

**Authorization Logic:**
1. Verify the requesting user has permission to view this promotion request's snapshots
2. Allow if user is the requester of the promotion request
3. Allow if user is an administrator (admin or superAdmin role)
4. Deny access for other users

**Response Structure:**
- Return paginated results using IPageIEcommerceMallAdminPromotionRequestSnapshot.Summary
- Include snapshot ID, timestamps, previous/new status, reviewer information, and reasons
- Resolve previousReviewer and newReviewer details from the admins table

**Edge Cases:**
- Empty list if promotion request has no status changes yet (only initial state)
- Handle case where previous_reviewer_id is null (first state change)
- Ensure proper handling of timezone in created_at timestamps

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific admin promotion request snapshot by its unique identifier.

This operation retrieves a single immutable snapshot record that captures the state of an admin promotion request at a specific point in time. Snapshots record state transitions such as when a promotion request is approved or rejected, preserving both the previous and new state values along with the reviewer identity responsible for the change.

**Authorization**: This operation is accessible to administrators and super administrators who have authority to view any snapshot on the platform for oversight and dispute resolution purposes.

**Data Structure**: The snapshot includes the parent promotion request reference, the administrator who reviewed before the change (previous_reviewer_id), the administrator who processed the current state change (new_reviewer_id), the status values before and after the transition (previous_status, new_status), the associated reasons or notes (previous_reason, new_reason), and the timestamp when this snapshot was created.

**Immutability**: Snapshots are immutable records that serve as the authoritative historical record for dispute resolution and audit trails. No modifications can be made to snapshot data after creation.

**Related Operations**: To view the list of snapshots for a promotion request, use the index endpoint. The parent promotion request must be identified first before accessing its snapshots.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the requesting user has administrator privileges (admin or superAdmin actor kind).

2. Extract path parameters:
   - promotionRequestId: UUID of the parent promotion request
   - snapshotId: UUID of the specific snapshot to retrieve

3. Query the ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots table:
   SELECT * FROM ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots 
   WHERE id = snapshotId 
   AND admin_promotion_request_id = promotionRequestId
   
   Note: The snapshot should exist under the given promotion request; if not found (either snapshot doesn't exist or belongs to different request), return 404.

4. If snapshot not found, return 404 Not Found error.

5. Transform database record to IEcommerceMallAdminPromotionRequestSnapshot DTO:
   - Include all fields: id, adminPromotionRequestId, previousReviewerId, newReviewerId, 
     previousStatus, newStatus, previousReason, newReason, createdAt
   - Previous and new reviewer IDs can be null if no reviewer was assigned
   - Reasons can be null if no reason was provided

6. Return the populated DTO in the response body.

7. Authorization check: All valid administrators can view any snapshot (no additional ownership check) per sections 412 and 590.

operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of seller registration applications for administrator review.

This operation allows administrators to view and filter seller registration requests submitted by prospective sellers. Administrators can filter registrations by status (pending, approved, rejected), submission date ranges, and other criteria to efficiently manage the approval workflow.

Each registration in the results includes the seller's information, current approval status, submission timestamp, and if applicable, the reviewer who processed it and any rejection reason provided. This supports the administrator review workflow described in requirements where administrators assess whether applicants meet platform standards.

The response is optimized for list display with essential information needed for quick evaluation. For detailed review and approval/rejection actions, administrators would use additional endpoints.

Authorization: Only administrators (admin, superAdmin) can access this endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations table with support for pagination and filtering.

Filter capabilities:
- status: Filter by registration status ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected')
- sellerId: Filter by specific seller
- reviewerId: Filter by administrator who reviewed
- createdAt range: Filter by submission date
- reviewedAt range: Filter by review date

Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers to include seller email and basic info in results.
Join with ecommerce_mall_admins (optional) to include reviewer details when available.

Sort options:
- created_at DESC (newest submissions first - default)
- created_at ASC (oldest first)
- reviewed_at DESC (recently reviewed)
- updated_at DESC (recent activity)

Return cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size.

Response includes:
- Registration id, status, rejection_reason
- Submission and review timestamps
- Seller summary (id, email)
- Reviewer summary if processed (id, nickname)

Exclude soft-deleted registrations unless specifically requested.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific seller registration by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a seller registration application, including the current approval status, submission timestamp, and review information if processed.

For sellers, this endpoint allows checking the status of their own registration application. The status can be one of three values:
- "pending": The application is awaiting administrator review
- "approved": The application has been approved, granting full seller privileges
- "rejected": The application was denied, with a reason provided

When administrators review registrations, they can use this endpoint to examine the full details of a specific application before making an approval or rejection decision.

If the registration status is "rejected", the response includes the rejection_reason field containing the administrator's explanation for the denial. Sellers can use this information when preparing a new registration submission.

The response includes related seller information and, if reviewed, the administrator who processed the application along with the review timestamp.

Security: Users can only access their own registrations unless they have administrator privileges.

Authorization checks:
1. If caller is a seller: verify that the seller_id on the registration matches the seller's ID
2. If caller is an admin (regular or super): allow access to any registration snapshot
3. If caller is a customer: deny access (only sellers and admins may view registration snapshots)

- id: The snapshot UUID
- sellerRegistrationId: References the parent registration
